bayts.text: I am well pleased with the Master, the Exalted, Who has nurtured my heart and enriched me; and how generous He is as Lord!
Through Him I have become rich today, His slave, through Him a servant perpetually of the one He chose as beloved.
Through Him I have become rich today, a slave, by His remembrance, and from me He holds back disgrace, the Fire and insult.
I have cast away idle talk for Allah, a slave reciting slowly a wise Remembrance (the Qurʾān): He has driven the enemies from my side.
I recite it slowly as long as I live and am content with it, and through it I drive Iblīs from me whenever he creeps.
To Him is my refuge, and He is the Enricher, the All-Embracing; His is the dominion and then the praise, and the state has already become firm.
I have come out, by the grace of Allah, from every falsehood, and parted from my (own) planning, through Him, in repelling and attracting.
I am well pleased with Him as a Generous, honouring Lord: He protected me from enemies, war, the sea and ruin.
My reward is with the Master, for my repelling the people of lies; and toward me they turned wealth, by His subjecting (them), without despoiling.
I have intended here the return to Ṭūbā (Touba), by His leave; and I have entrusted Him with my body and entrusted Him with the heart.
To Allah and the Chosen have I emigrated, from a throng whose acts of worship are disobedience to the Lord of creation, the Gracious.
My aim is granted me by a Lord Who brings forward, Eternal, Whose dominion has encompassed the east and the west.
My deliverance from enemies, the sea and trial, a stranger, alone, (came) from a Guardian Who filled the satchels.
The Exalted guided me after I had nearly perished, by the standing of him who adorned non-Arabs and Arabs.
I converse with Him intimately in secret and openly, and I hope for my righteousness and my reforming, through Him, of family and peers.
I humbled myself before Him, not before the enemies; then there was for me, as a treasure, a Book whose love dispels distress.
My Lord guided me through it, and I guide by its light, when the Lord wills, the far and the near.
My God, lead me to my Ṭūbā (Touba) and keep me safe, and bestow favour there, and make the land secure.
Yours are the land and the sea, to which You led me; on land grant me safety and honour (my) side.
Turn the hearts of the enemies toward what gladdens me, and through me give glad tidings to the elect, and forgive the sin.
I have hoped for my parting forever from all the enemies, and meeting my family, from You, O You Who fulfilled the needs.
Your subduing might, Lord, overturns their hearts: so be for me with "Be", Lord, and widen the enclosure for me.
Favour me today, O Lord, with the wishes, with an opening and an outpouring that put the pouring downpour to shame.
To You and to the Chosen I emigrated with guidance and with the radiant Sunna, O You Who protected from perdition.
Turn toward me the cups of the folk (of saints) and give me to drink with them, and widen and grant me the sip, O Lord, and the deep draught.
My darknesses, by the Lamp (the Prophet), You dispelled from me — upon him a blessing from You — by which I may contain love.
You removed through him my arrogance and my self-satisfaction, nurturing — upon him a peace from You — that spares me deceit.
You have already driven to me at sea what I hoped for, by the standing of him whom You made the intimate and the beloved.
You effaced my fault through him: so lead me away from the enemies to my brothers, and make my return a remedy for us.
You granted protection to the one who hoped for protection: so increase him in guidance and knowledge, and spare him self-conceit.
You guided the one whom his ignorance was about to ruin: so remove from him the veils, O Lord, and the curtains.
To You be gratitude, good pleasure and praise forever, and I have no doubt that You are Allah and the Lord.
I forsook idle talk with remembrance and gratitude, praising the Chosen, he whose bounty has poured toward me.
O Allah, O All-Merciful (Ar-Raḥmān), O You Who succoured me: so bless with peace the best of those who answered "Labbayka".
I have trusted: be for me, through the Followed (al-Muqaffā), his Family and his Companions, those who put the lion to shame when it roared.
They were granted the reward of Allah in every campaign, with love, good pleasure, nearness and kinship.
Their struggle (jihād) is deeds, in truth, and each of them the Effacer (al-Māḥī) gladdens with tidings when he faced war.
Upon them, from the Master, good pleasure and mercy, as they removed misfortune from me with their swords.
Through them, O my King, make for me the best way out, and make good, preserve, grant favour and increase longing.
Write for him a blessing with peace, through them together, and grant me through them, O my King, the folding (of the path) and the (divine) attraction.
I have cast away what I sold: so replace it (with better), and keep me far from self-conceit, arrogance and lying.
Grant me charisms (karāmāt), and be for me without end with what surpasses my expectation, and subject the difficult to me.
I have stretched out my hand, O my King, hoping in You, a stranger, penitent: grant me comfort and lift the terror.
You have repelled harm from me: so grant me my return, swift, without toil, and widen the road for me.
To You be gratitude, since You made me the servant of the Prophet — upon him a blessing from You — by which You exalt the Companions.
I have called upon You through the Chosen, through all the Family and his Companions, O You Who through them spared me adversity.
You repelled harm from me through them, then You were for me: so make the return good for me and make plenty eternal for me.
You spared me the upholders of the Trinity, and they turned back, singly and in pairs: spare me them through them always.
I have trusted in You, O Allah, (for) my request and my desires, perpetually, by the standing of the Chosen; and spare me grief.
Write for him a blessing with peace, with his Family and his Companions, and make my mosque spacious through him.
My good opinion (of God) gives him glad tidings, which led me to supplication: so give glad tidings to whoever prolonged weeping for me.
My knowledge of Your being Powerful over all things gives him glad tidings: answer me and spare me calamity.
Answer my supplication, turn outpourings toward all of me, and make my outpourings eternal and do not leave off the pouring.
I have trusted in an Everlasting, Subduing, Powerful One, to Whom belong my heart and my body, and Who accepts my earning for me.
I shall keep up for Him, as long as I live, if He wills, worship, and I hope from Him an acceptance that bequeaths abundance.
I have made the Book of Allah my daily litany, and I seek, by reciting it slowly, what I have willed, as a lasting pasture for me.
I owe my Lord the debt of slow recitation of His verses, and I return to my people with it, as pasture.
To my Lord be my praise and then gratitude without end, for making my breast the vessel of His verses, portion by portion (ḥizb).
To Him — exalted be He — be my gratitude after praise; and He has been for me, and tamed for me enemies who, in a band, had made for my side.
I was saved, by the keeping of Allah, from the onslaught of the enemies, and He tamed them all for me, and honoured my side.
The Tender (Al-Ḥannān) succoured me from the plot of whoever hated, and the sea became for me, like the fire of the Intimate Friend (Abraham, Qurʾān 21:69), a thing that does not harm.
My ink, my pens, my tablet, all of me and my body belong to Him Who turned keeping and gift toward me.
I have intended for Him abundant gratitude, as He protected my side, and I ask Him to spare me, on the day of burning, the flame.
To Him — exalted be He — be my gratitude, since He guided me by His grace and by the standing of him whose praise by me has become for me a cutting sword.
He called me to the Abode of Peace (Qurʾān 10:25), in which I converse with Him intimately with the remembrance that made the heart good.
He repelled Satan from me, who turned back with his plot; and I seek salvation from him, (with) Him, whenever he creeps.
A Guardian, Subduer, Preventer has spared me, here, doubts and whisperings, and driven the enemies from me.
I have intended a return endowed with blessing, greeting with peace the Chosen, the Effacer, whom He chose as beloved.
Blessing and peace upon the Chosen, the Prophet, with the Family and the Companions, (from) Him Who repelled deceit.
May a Lord, a Guardian Who spared perdition, bless him with peace, with his Family and his Companions,
Merciful, Appreciative, from Whom I hope He will raise my writings to Himself; and how generous He is as Lord!
I bless him with peace, for the Countenance of Him Who through him drives to me what He chose for me, as He has nurtured me.
